narrative.overview:
Social is a DJ booth, not a chat app or a card feed. Every member is a deck: their current or last cover spins on a dark platter inside a progress ring, with their name plate, state line and dated last listen beside it. The page opens on who is playing what: a featured deck with the track's real waveform and a live playhead, a shelf of other decks receding by recency, then the composer and the track log. Messages collapses the booth into a strip of discs and keeps the messenger fundamentals (list, thread, docked composer, details panel).

The material is matte black and deliberately colorless. The surface has no hue of its own: chroma comes only from the artwork, read from each cover at runtime and spilled as symmetric light, ring color, waveform gradient and conversation tint. Exactly two fixed hues exist, each with one meaning: presence green for someone here now, like-red for a liked post. Depth is three plies only: the page ground, inset panels, floating overlays.

Motion is the room being alive, never decoration: platters spin at 7.2s per turn only while their member plays, rings and playheads advance on real time, layout moves on one ease-out curve, and a springy overshoot is reserved for tactile gestures. Everything is off under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Members rendered as decks: cover disc, progress ring, rim marker, name plate, state line, dated last listen
Featured deck and shelf side by side at 1.38fr : 1fr (about 58/42), stacking below a 1060px container
Recency as depth: older listens shrink, desaturate and dim; silent members sit at an avatar-only edge
Artwork is the only source of color; it never marks state
Real waveforms decoded from the audio, tinted by the cover, readable on dark covers
Three plies: ground, 16px inset panels on hairlines, opaque floating overlays
Container queries on `#page-social`, never viewport media queries, for layout
Keyed DOM patching so live updates never restart a spinning deck or replay an entrance
Chrome hidden until hover or focus on decks and messages; states stamp, strikes draw

rules.name: The Artwork-Only Chroma Rule
rules.body: The surface owns no hue. Every chromatic pixel outside the two signal colors is read from a cover; never pick a decorative accent.

rules.name: The Cover-Never-Marks-State Rule
rules.body: A cover's color says what is playing, never whether someone is live, unread, selected or followed. State is ink, wash, or presence green.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Presence green means a human is here now; like-red means liked. Neither appears anywhere else, and no other hue may carry a state.

rules.name: The Tabular Readout Rule
rules.body: Every number that reads as time, position or count uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so live readouts never jitter.

rules.name: The Switzer Is a Label Rule
rules.body: Switzer appears only at headline sizes and above; it never sets body, names or controls.

rules.name: The Container Knows Rule
rules.body: Layout responds to `@container social`, never a viewport media query.

rules.name: The Recency-Is-Depth Rule
rules.body: Distance in the booth is time since the last listen, on the `boothDepth` ladder. Never size or fade a deck for any other reason.

rules.name: The Clip-Not-Hide Rule
rules.body: Panes, slots, strips and rows use `overflow: clip`, never `hidden`, so focusing a field can never scroll a pane sideways. Rows that scroll (shelf, strip) fade only on the side that still hides decks (`--fade-start` / `--fade-end`).

rules.name: The Three Plies Rule
rules.body: Ground, inset panel, floating overlay. Never nest a panel in a panel to make a fourth ply; group with rules and spacing instead.

rules.name: The Symmetric Light Rule
rules.body: Cover light is a centered radial around the disc and fades before the panel edge. No directional or offset glows.

dos: **Do** express every neutral through theme tokens or the `--booth-*` mixes; `#5ee890` and `#ff5470` are the only fixed hues.
**Do** read color from the artwork into `--deck-color` or `--tint`, and fall back to ink.
**Do** place every member on the `boothDepth` ladder and keep their fixed furniture: name plate, state line, dated last listen.
**Do** draw waveforms from real decoded peaks, cached once per track, with the dynamic-range stretch and the 0.56 lightness floor.
**Do** use `@container social` for every layout change, and `overflow: clip` on panes and rows.
**Do** keep the spring for tactile keyframe gestures and the ease-out curve for everything else, and register new motion in the reduced-motion block.
**Do** patch lists by key so a spinning deck never restarts.
**Do** write class names as literals in JS (`'is-near'`, never `` `is-${band}` ``) so PurgeCSS keeps them.
**Do** use `tabular-nums` on every time, position and count.
donts: **Don't** let a cover color mark state (live, unread, selected, followed).
**Don't** use presence green for anything but presence, or like-red for anything but likes.
**Don't** add a fourth ply: no panel inside a panel, no shadow on a resting inset panel.
**Don't** cast directional or offset glows; cover light is symmetric and stops before the panel edge.
**Don't** fake waveforms with random or placeholder bars.
**Don't** put a spindle through an avatar, or send a member to the edge unless they have no listen within 30 days (never "You").
**Don't** name whole views for view transitions.
**Don't** show deck actions or the message pin at rest; they appear on hover or focus.
